title: Albatross Soup
story: A man tastes albatross soup at a restaurant and repeatedly asks the chef what meat it contains. After hearing the answer, he pays and leaves. That night he takes his own life. The soup is not poisoned and the chef has told the truth. Why?
answer: Years before, the man and his wife were shipwrecked. She died on a deserted island. A companion fed the starving man some meat, claiming it was albatross. On tasting genuine albatross soup after his rescue, he realized the island meat had tasted entirely different. He questioned his companion and learned he had eaten his wife's body. Unable to bear the truth, he died by suicide.
hints: He and his wife were once stranded on an island, where she died.
A fellow survivor served him meat described as seabird.
After his rescue, that survivor admitted the meat had come from his wife.

title: Half a Match
story: A man is found dead from a fall in the desert. He is naked and holds half an unburned match. Clothes and luggage lie nearby, but there is no wreckage of a plane. Why?
answer: He and his companions were losing altitude in a hot-air balloon. They threw out their luggage and then their clothes, but kept falling. They drew matches to decide who would jump and lighten the balloon. The man drew the shortened match and kept their agreement. He fell to his death.
hints: He was in a descending hot-air balloon with other passengers.
They discarded luggage and clothing to reduce the load.
Unequal matches were used to draw lots for who must leave the basket.

title: After the Light Went Out
story: A man turns off a light before bed. The next morning he sees wreckage in the distance and knows that many strangers died because of him. He never left his home that night. Why?
answer: He was a lighthouse keeper and had switched off the light guiding ships at night. Without that landmark, a vessel struck a nearby reef and many people died. The wreckage at sea showed him the consequences of turning it off.
hints: His job involved guiding ships at night.
Dangerous rocks lay in the nearby waters.
The ship lost its navigational beacon when the light went out and struck the rocks.

title: When the Music Stopped
story: The music stopped suddenly. A woman took one step and fell to her death. Nobody touched her or asked her to die. Why?
answer: She was walking a high wire blindfolded, without a safety net. She and the band had agreed that the music would stop only when she reached the end platform. The band stopped early by mistake. Believing she had reached solid ground, she stepped off the wire into empty air.
hints: She was performing high above the ground while blindfolded.
She and the musicians used silence to signal arrival at the platform.
She was on a tightrope without a safety net; the musicians stopped too early.

title: The Slow Drinker
story: Two people drink iced tea poured from the same pot. One quickly finishes several glasses; the other slowly drinks just one. The slow drinker dies from poison, while the fast drinker survives. Why?
answer: The poison was in the ice cubes. The fast drinker finished before much ice melted and left the cubes behind. In the slow drinker's glass, the ice gradually melted into the tea and released a lethal dose. Timing, not the tea in the pot, made the difference.
hints: The tea in the pot was safe; poison was in something added to the cups.
The fast drinker left most of the ice behind before it melted.
The slow drinker's melting ice released poison into the tea.

title: The Rewound Farewell
story: A man lies dead beside a gun and a cassette recorder. An officer presses Play once and hears his farewell followed by a gunshot. After listening, the officer investigates who arranged the scene. Why?
answer: The recorder could only be rewound manually. A murderer forced the man to record a farewell, killed him, then rewound the tape so whoever arrived would hear a supposed suicide note. Since the recording included the fatal gunshot yet began at the farewell when the officer pressed Play, someone must have handled the machine after the death.
hints: This recorder could not rewind automatically.
The fatal shot was recorded; afterward the victim could no longer operate the machine.
Someone forced him to record a farewell and handled the tape after killing him.

title: A Ticket with No Return
story: News of a tourist falling into the sea makes a ticket agent put down his breakfast. He does not know the dead woman, yet calls the police and says someone knew before departure that she would never return. Why?
answer: He remembered the woman's husband buying a round-trip ticket for himself but only a one-way ticket for her, even while saying they would travel home together. After hearing that she had fallen into the sea, the agent gave police the purchase records as a clue that the husband had planned her death.
hints: The husband bought both travelers' tickets before departure.
He told the seller that they planned to return together.
Only he had a return ticket; his wife's was one-way.

title: The Old Pact on the Train
story: A one-armed man recognizes an old friend on a subway train. When the friend raises both hands in greeting, the man shoots him. They once survived the same disaster. Why?
answer: They had been shipwrecked with others. Facing starvation, they agreed that each would sacrifice an arm for food in turn. Rescue came just before the final man's turn. He fled and refused to honor the terrible pact. Years later the one-armed survivor recognized him, saw that he still had both arms, and killed him out of resentment.
hints: They once survived a shipwreck and were stranded without food.
The survivors agreed to sacrifice an arm each in turn to feed the others.
Rescue arrived before the friend's turn; he fled afterward and refused to honor the pact.

title: Happy Birthday Behind the Door
story: A man kills his wife outside their home, then opens the door. The lights come on and a crowd shouts 'Happy birthday!' He had planned to flee the city, but collapses on the spot. Why?
answer: He believed the house was empty and intended to escape after killing his wife. She had arranged a surprise party: friends and family waited silently inside in the dark. As he dragged her body through the door, they switched on the lights and witnessed the scene. His escape plan was exposed.
hints: His wife organized the gathering without telling him.
At her invitation, friends and relatives had hidden inside.
When the lights came on, he was dragging her body through the doorway.

title: The Only Dark Room
story: Late at night, a man in a motel parking lot keeps honking his horn. Window after window lights up, except one room. He apologizes, goes to the dark room, and finds his wife. Why?
answer: He had gone out to the car and forgotten their room number. The small motel was full and every room looked alike. His wife was deaf and still asleep inside. The horn woke the other guests, who switched on their lights to see what was happening. Her room stayed dark, so he knew which one was theirs.
hints: He had gone to his car and forgotten his room number on returning.
His wife was deaf and asleep in their room.
The motel was full, and all the other guests turned on their lights to investigate the noise.

title: The Pack That Never Opened
story: A dead man lies in an open field with an unopened pack on his back. There are no vehicles or footprints leading toward him. The people who find him say the pack could have saved him. Why?
answer: He jumped from an aircraft, but his parachute malfunctioned and never opened. The pack was the parachute container. There were no approaching footprints because he arrived from the sky.
hints: An accident occurred during his descent after leaving an aircraft.
The pack was meant to slow his fall through the air.
Its parachute failed to deploy.

title: The Winner Died First
story: Through a window I see two dead people, scattered playing cards, and a gun. One was shot; the other drowned. The winner of their last game was the one who was shot. Why?
answer: I am a diver looking into a cabin of a sunken ship. As it flooded, two people were trapped with a gun holding one bullet. Terrified of drowning, they played cards to decide who would use the bullet and die quickly. The winner was shot; the other later drowned as water filled the cabin.
hints: The witness was a diver examining a wreck.
The men were trapped in a flooding cabin with only one bullet.
The game decided who could use the bullet to avoid drowning.

title: The Bartender's Gun
story: A customer asks for water. The bartender points a gun at him. After a moment, the customer says thanks and leaves without drinking.
answer: The customer wanted water for his hiccups. Hearing them, the bartender frightened him with a gun. In this story, the fright stopped the hiccups, so he left grateful.
hints: He wanted relief from a physical discomfort.
The bartender noticed interruptions in his speech.
The fright stopped the symptom.

title: The Rainy-Day Elevator
story: A man lives on floor ten. Alone on dry days, he takes the elevator to seven and walks the rest. On rainy days he rides to ten. He always rides straight down.
answer: He is short and can reach only the lower buttons. The ground-floor button is accessible. His umbrella lets him press ten on rainy days.
hints: Higher floors have higher buttons.
His reach is limited by his height.
Rain means he carries an umbrella.

title: Antony and Cleopatra
story: Antony and Cleopatra lie dead beside water and broken glass. Neither has wounds or was poisoned. A dog is the only witness.
answer: They were goldfish. The dog knocked over their bowl, which shattered. Without water, the fish died.
hints: The dog toppled a glass container of water.
The victims lived inside that container.
Their breathing depended on oxygen in water.

title: The Silent Call
story: Unable to sleep, a man makes a phone call. When someone answers, he hangs up without speaking. He can finally fall asleep.
answer: A guest next door was snoring. He called that hotel room to wake the guest, stopping the noise long enough to fall asleep.
hints: Noise from the neighboring hotel room kept him awake.
The person answering was making that noise.
The ringing woke a snoring guest.

title: Rewarded and Fired
story: A night watchman dreams of a plane crash and warns his employer. The employer cancels the flight, which crashes. He rewards the watchman, then fires him.
answer: The dream occurred during the watchman's shift. His warning earned gratitude, but sleeping when he should have been guarding the premises cost him his job.
hints: The dream happened during his shift.
His duties required him to stay awake.
The reward and dismissal concerned different actions.

title: The Sawdust
story: A man dies. Some sawdust in his room could have saved him, but he never noticed it. What would it have revealed?
answer: A blind circus performer earned his living from his unusually short stature. A rival shortened his cane. Mistaking the change for his own growth, he feared losing his livelihood and took his life. The sawdust would have exposed the tampering.
hints: He relied on touch because he was blind.
His circus livelihood depended on his short stature.
A rival had altered his wooden cane.

title: A Light in the Tunnel
story: A train enters a tunnel. A passenger loses hope and considers taking his life. A tiny distant glow changes his mind, though it does not illuminate the exit.
answer: Returning from surgery that restored his sight, he mistook the unlit carriage's darkness for renewed blindness. A passenger's glowing cigarette showed him that he could still see.
hints: He was returning from eye surgery.
The carriage had no internal lighting.
The glow came from a cigarette and proved his sight remained.

title: The Empty Room
story: A man hangs dead in a windowless room locked from within. There is no furniture or ladder beneath him, only water. What happened to his support?
answer: His support had been a block of ice. It melted after his death, leaving the puddle.
hints: A solid object had supported his weight.
The room's warmth changed that object's state.
The puddle is what remains of the support.

title: The Fifty-Third Card
story: A man lies dead beside a card table. There are fifty-three playing cards and no jokers. Counting them reveals the cause of the quarrel.
answer: The game used a single fifty-two-card deck. The man had smuggled in an extra card to cheat. Other players discovered it and killed him.
hints: The game used one deck with the jokers removed.
The victim had concealed an extra card.
The other gamblers discovered his cheating.

title: The Mountain Cabin
story: Two uniformed men are dead in a cabin on a mountainside. There are signs of fire nearby, but both died before it started. What happened?
answer: The cabin is the cockpit of a crashed aircraft. The pilots died in the impact, before the fire.
hints: Their uniforms indicate that they worked here in the same profession.
The cabin was part of a vehicle.
A fatal impact preceded the fire.

title: Another Funeral
story: A woman falls for a stranger at her mother's funeral but gets no contact details. Days later she kills her sister. Why?
answer: She hopes another family funeral will bring the stranger back. She kills her sister to create that occasion.
hints: She wants to see the stranger again.
Her sister's death will cause another family gathering.
She expects some of the same mourners to return.

title: The Pointing Finger
story: From my lit room, I see a murder across the street. The killer notices me, then moves his finger along my building, floor by floor. My fear grows.
answer: He is counting floors and windows to locate the witness. He intends to come to my room and silence me.
hints: He sees me as a witness he must silence.
His finger follows the building's windows in sequence.
He intends to visit the room he identifies.

title: The Cabin Portraits
story: Lost in a forest, a hunter sleeps in an empty cabin. Realistic faces on the walls unsettle him. By daylight they are gone, and he realizes the danger he was in.
answer: He mistook windows for framed portraits. People outside had been looking in. Daylight revealed the windows after the watchers left.
hints: Daylight enters where the faces appeared.
The frames were part of the building.
The faces belonged to watchers outside.

title: The Fatal Ring
story: A husband phones his wife. Before she can answer, the call causes someone to kill her. Her husband meant no harm and knew nothing of the danger.
answer: She was hiding from an intruder at home. Her unsilenced phone rang, revealing her hiding place to the killer.
hints: She was hiding from an intruder.
Her phone was with her, with its ringer on.
The intruder located her by sound.

title: Five in the Rain
story: Five people head to church. Rain starts; four run and get soaked. The fifth takes no steps but arrives with them, dry.
answer: Four pallbearers carry a coffin. The fifth person is the deceased inside it, sheltered from the rain.
hints: Four people carry a large covered object.
The fifth travels inside it.
They are going to a funeral.

title: The Last Body in the Well
story: Whenever a killer throws a victim into a well, the body disappears by morning. Then he kills his mother and throws her in. This body remains.
answer: His mother had secretly removed the other bodies to conceal his crimes. With her dead, nobody continued the cover-up.
hints: Someone visited the well after he left.
That person knowingly concealed his crimes.
His mother had been doing the cleanup.

title: The Missing Bride
story: A bride vanishes during a wedding game of hide-and-seek. Guests think she ran away. Years later, opening a chest in the house reveals she never left.
answer: She hid in an attic chest whose lid locked shut. Unable to open it from inside and never found, she died there. Her remains were discovered years later.
hints: She went to the attic during the game.
Her hiding place was an old chest.
The closed lid locked, with no release inside.

title: The Choice of Pills
story: A kidnapper offers two identical pills, claiming one is poisoned. The hostage chooses first; he takes the other. Both swallow with their own water. Only the hostage dies, every time.
answer: Both pills are harmless sugar pills. The hostage's water is poisoned; the kidnapper's water is safe. Choosing pills cannot change the outcome.
hints: One of the kidnapper's claims about the pills is a lie.
Both pills are harmless sugar pills.
The hostage's water contains the poison.
